whatItIs.text: A thin, circular unleavened flatbread — corn (from nixtamalized masa) or wheat flour — the everyday bread of Mexico and Central America and the wrap of half the world.

historyNote.text: Tortillas were made by the ancient peoples of Mesoamerica, where the Aztecs called them tlaxcalli; flour versions only appeared after the Spanish brought wheat to Mexico, and mass production took off in the 1950s with tortilla machines and masa harina.

howToChoose.text: Corn tortillas for authentic taco flavour and a lower-fat base; flour for burrito flexibility. Fresh tortilleria or refrigerated packs beat shelf-stable stacks every time.

storage.text: Keep sealed at room temperature for days or the fridge for longer.

foodSafetyRef.note: Practice storage guidance only; no rulebook content is claimed. The app's food-safety rules live in data/food-safety/rules.json.

useItUp.text: Stale tortillas are raw material: fry or bake them into chips and tostadas, tear them into tortilla soup, or blitz into crumbs for coating.
